newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to make Dassault announcement in January.
newsitem.headline: France to make Dassault announcement in January.

text.p: The French government plans to announce in early January how it will merge state-owned Aerospatiale with combat-plane maker Dassault Aviation, a defence ministry official said on Friday.
"We're on track with the timetable," the official said. "We should be able to make an announcement in early January on how the merger between the two will be carried out."
The official said negotiations between the two were not yet completed on the merger but talks were progressing well.
The official's comments followed a report in the newspaper Le Monde which said Defence Minister Charles Millon would announce the setting up of the merged group early next year.
The newspaper said talks were still continuing with the state on the financial aspects of the merger.
A Dassault official confirmed that Aerospatiale and Dassault earlier this week submitted a plan setting out the industrial organisation for the merger, as reported in newspapers.

Earlier this week, Industry Minister Franck Borotra called for a speeding up of the merger to meet the challenge posed by the linkup between Boeing-McDonnell Douglas creating the world's biggest aerospace company.
The centre-right government had given the two companies until the end of the year to seal the details of their merger.
But Aerospatiale said last summer it thought legal formalities would drag out the process and that the new company would not start-up until mid-1997 at the earliest.

The government sought the merger between the two pillars of France's aerospace industry to improve the country's ability to compete with other national aerospace industries and increase opportunities with the rest of Europe on defence ventures.
